turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please sit. You look worn out — what's been the trouble?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): This cough. Six weeks now, worse at night, and I am properly fed up.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Six weeks, and worse at night. Did a flu start it?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya. Fever, body ache, the usual flu. Fever went, the cough stayed.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fever now, then?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Just tired, and snappy with everyone.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the cough dry, or do you bring up phlegm?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly dry. A little white phlegm in the morning, nothing else.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in that phlegm?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): At night I am not getting any sleep. And the traffic coming here was too much. I almost went back home.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the traffic. Any blood, even a small streak?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. Hardly any phlegm, I said.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Apart from night-time, what makes it worse or better?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Lying flat is worse, so I sit up. Warm water helps a little. That's all.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any breathlessness, or chest pain?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): On the stairs to the third floor I get a bit short of breath. Pain, no.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight loss?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No weight loss. I am eating fine. Don't start with that.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Night sweats? Feeling cold?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No sweats. I feel a bit cold when the cough starts. Can we please hurry, I have to get back to the office.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Short as I can. Recent travel, or contact with anyone who has tuberculosis?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No travel. Only home and office. I have not left the city.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the TB contact — anyone at home, or at work?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No one. I keep away from all that.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Though Amma rang about a cousin in Nagpur. He was in hospital, and she said TB. I have not met him in years, so there is no contact from my side, and I don't even know if she heard it right.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): So I'll take it as no travel and no contact you can stand by; the cousin part is only hearsay. Medicines you've used?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist gave azithromycin, five hundred milligrams, once a day. I was going to say three days — no, it was five days. I finished it around two weeks back. It did nothing.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not on it now. What are you still taking?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ambroxol syrup, ten ml at night, for this cough. And telmisartan, forty milligrams, every morning for my BP, since three years.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any drug, or to anything else?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped ten years back. Before that, eight or sometimes ten a day.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me listen. Lungs are clear, no wheeze, no crackles. Your throat is mildly red. Saturation is ninety-seven percent, pulse eighty-eight, temperature thirty-six point eight, blood pressure one twenty-eight over eighty-two, and you're breathing at eighteen.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Then what is it? Say it plain. I am too tired for all this roundabout talk.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not going to name a cause today. A cough can drag on after flu, but six weeks is long enough. I am ordering a chest X-ray today.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Only an X-ray? These days everyone says do a scan.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): No scan now. If the cough has not settled in two weeks, we might do a CT. Let's see you back in two weeks, with the X-ray.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks more of this. Lovely.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the ambroxol at night, sleep sitting up a bit, take warm fluids, and don't start another antibiotic. You denied weight loss — have the clothes got loose?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah. The trousers have become loose. The belt is in by two holes. Maybe four or five kilos, I really don't know.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clothes looser, quantity unclear. Putting it together: six weeks of cough after flu, worse at night and lying down, mild breathlessness on stairs, fever gone, no blood, no night sweats, no travel, no TB contact you can confirm. Chest X-ray today, review in two weeks, CT only if it hasn't settled.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Just send me for the X-ray. I want to go home and sleep.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Sitting up is not stated as relieving; only lying flat worsens and warm water helps.
bad.text: cough (category=respiratory, status=present, duration=6 weeks, onset=after a flu, temporality=current, aggravating_factors=night and lying flat, relieving_factors=warm water and sitting up, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Current fever was specifically denied: 'No fever now.'

Weight loss was initially denied but later revised: patient said trousers had become loose, belt in by two holes, maybe 4–5 kg; the recorded fact 'loose clothes' misses that this contradicts the earlier denial and suggests possible weight loss.
Azithromycin course was finished around two weeks ago and the patient said it 'did nothing'; current record notes discontinued but misses timing and lack of effect.
Patient has not left the city; this adds detail to the denied recent travel history.

Possible TB history was discussed: mother mentioned a cousin in Nagpur was hospitalized and may have had TB, but patient has not met him in years and is unsure if the report was correct. This hearsay/uncertain non-contact is not captured.
Doctor explicitly said he was not naming a cause/diagnosis today.
Planned follow-up was specifically to return in two weeks with the chest X-ray.
